balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For IQVIA Holdings Inc.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For IQVIA Holdings Inc.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For IQVIA Holdings Inc.: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For IQVIA Holdings Inc.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For IQVIA Holdings Inc.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For IQVIA Holdings Inc.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For IQVIA Holdings Inc.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For IQVIA Holdings Inc.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For IQVIA Holdings Inc.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For IQVIA Holdings Inc.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue

segmentRevenueOld.title: Segment revenue (legacy scheme, through FY2025)
segmentRevenueOld.content:
Through FY2025 IQVIA reported three segments: Technology & Analytics Solutions (TAS) (data, software and analytics), Research & Development Solutions (R&DS) (the CRO -- clinical trial execution, the largest and highest-margin segment), and Contract Sales & Medical Solutions (CSMS) (outsourced commercial field teams, small and historically thin-margin).

For IQVIA Holdings Inc.: R&DS funds the group; CSMS has been shrinking for years and was folded into the new Commercial Solutions segment in the Q1 2026 reorganization.

What to watch:

  • R&DS revenue growth -- the biopharma R&D funding cycle drives it
  • This series stops at Q1 2025 (last comparative disclosure); see the new-scheme chart for current data

segmentRevenueNew.title: Segment revenue (new scheme, from Q1 2026)
segmentRevenueNew.content:
Effective Q1 2026 IQVIA collapsed its reporting to two segments: Commercial Solutions (legacy TAS + CSMS combined) and a recast R&DS that additionally absorbed the Real-World & Late Phase Research business out of the old TAS. The recast R&DS is therefore larger than the old R&DS line and not directly comparable to it.

For IQVIA Holdings Inc.: management gave Q1-Q3 2025 comparatives on the new basis, which is why this series starts in 2025 rather than exactly at the Q1 2026 cutover.

What to watch:

  • R&DS (recast) growth as the clearest read on CRO demand
  • Whether Commercial Solutions, combining two previously separate low/high-margin businesses, grows or just dilutes the mix

segmentMarginNew.title: Segment profit margin (new scheme)
segmentMarginNew.content:
Segment profit (management's operating-income measure by segment) divided by segment revenue, for the two post-reorganization segments only. The legacy TAS/R&DS/CSMS margins are not shown here to avoid mixing non-comparable segment definitions in one line -- see the revenue help for why.

For IQVIA Holdings Inc.: R&DS (recast) has consistently run a higher margin than Commercial Solutions; a narrowing gap would say the CRO business is losing its pricing power, not that Commercial Solutions is improving.

What to watch:

  • R&DS (recast) margin trend versus the overall company margin
  • Commercial Solutions margin, since it blends a software/analytics business with field-force services

backlog.title: Backlog and near-term convertible backlog
backlog.content:
Backlog is the dollar value of signed contracts not yet recognized as revenue -- overwhelmingly R&DS (CRO) business, since trial contracts run for years. Converting within 12 months is management's own estimate of how much of that backlog becomes revenue in the next year, the figure analysts watch most closely as a leading indicator.

For IQVIA Holdings Inc.: backlog growth lags bookings and leads revenue by roughly a year; FY2025's backlog was also restated to $34.0bn under the new segment scheme (BacklogRecast, a single data point, not charted as a series) -- the bars here use the as-originally-reported total throughout.

What to watch:

  • 12-month convertible backlog growth versus trailing revenue growth -- a widening gap signals an accelerating or decelerating pipeline before it shows up in revenue
  • Cancellations, which reduce backlog without ever hitting revenue
